vocabulary.meaning_en: the possibility that something will happen
vocabulary.example: There's a good chance of rain today.
Is there any possibility of a discount?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a show on TV or radio
vocabulary.example: I watched a programme about the ocean.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an ability to do something well
to share information or ideas with others
admiring something because it is good
vocabulary.example: I was impressed by her English.

vocabulary.meaning_en: too much excitement or worry about something small
vocabulary.example: Why all the fuss about a small mistake?

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that is your duty or fault
vocabulary.example: Cleaning the room is your responsibility.
The difference in price is insignificant.

vocabulary.meaning_en: small round pieces of metal money
vocabulary.example: I need some coins for the parking machine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: clever; able to learn and understand quickly
saying the opposite of what you mean to criticise or joke
vocabulary.example: "Great weather!" he said in a sarcastic voice when it rained.
We had a nice conversation on the train.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who tries to make others admire them

vocabulary.example: In the Netherlands, some people wear wooden clogs.

fine_lines.title: small change vs small talk
fine_lines.explanation_ar: small change: النقود المعدنية الصغيرة، أو شيء تافه غير مهم مقارنة بغيره. small talk: حديث خفيف عن أمور غير مهمة (الطقس مثلاً) مع أشخاص لا تعرفهم جيداً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Small change' means coins, or something unimportant compared with something else. 'Small talk' is polite, light conversation about unimportant things, like the weather.

examples.sentence: My cold is small change compared with your broken arm.
We made small talk while we waited for the lift.

fine_lines.title: a bright spark vs clever clogs
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a bright spark: شخص ذكي ونشيط، لكنها تُستخدم كثيراً بسخرية لمن جاء بفكرة غبية: Which bright spark...? أما clever clogs: شخص مزعج يتصرف وكأنه يعرف أكثر من الجميع.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'A bright spark' is a clever, lively person, but it is often used sarcastically for someone with a silly idea: 'Which bright spark...?' A 'clever clogs' is an annoying person who acts as if they know more than everyone.

examples.sentence: Which bright spark left the door open in the rain?
OK, clever clogs, you answer the question then.

fine_lines.title: big deal: two uses
fine_lines.explanation_ar: Big deal! وحدها تعني «وماذا في ذلك؟ لست منبهراً». أما make a big deal about something فتعني يثير ضجة كبيرة حول أمر صغير.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Big deal!' on its own means 'So what? I'm not impressed.' 'Make a big deal about something' means make a big fuss.

examples.sentence: You got a new phone? Big deal – everyone has one.
Don't make a big deal about it – it was only a small mistake.

expressions.meaning_en: very little chance; often said to mean 'no way'
expressions.example: He'll clean his room without being asked? Fat chance!

expressions.meaning_ar: برامج تلفزيونية طويلة وهادئة تعرض حدثاً عادياً كاملاً (رحلة قطار مثلاً)
expressions.meaning_en: long, calm TV programmes that show an ordinary event from start to finish
expressions.example: I watched four hours of slow TV about a boat trip – it was very relaxing.

expressions.meaning_ar: مهارات التواصل والتعامل والعمل مع الآخرين
expressions.meaning_en: the ability to communicate and work well with other people
expressions.example: The job needs good soft skills, like teamwork and listening.

expressions.meaning_ar: وماذا في ذلك؟ (لست منبهراً)؛ وأيضاً: أمر مهم
expressions.meaning_en: said to show you are not impressed; also something important
expressions.example: You ran 2 km? Big deal – I ran 10!

expressions.meaning_en: to make a big fuss about something
expressions.example: She made a big deal about her birthday.

expressions.meaning_en: informal: sorry, it was my mistake
expressions.example: My bad – I took your pen by mistake.

expressions.meaning_ar: نقود معدنية صغيرة؛ أو شيء تافه غير مهم
expressions.meaning_en: coins; or something not important compared with something else
expressions.example: This problem is small change compared with last year's.

expressions.meaning_ar: شخص ذكي ونشيط؛ وغالباً بسخرية لمن فعل شيئاً غبياً
expressions.meaning_en: a clever, lively person; often used sarcastically
expressions.example: Which bright spark turned off the fridge?

expressions.meaning_ar: حديث خفيف عن أمور عامة غير مهمة
expressions.example: I'm not good at small talk with people I don't know.

expressions.meaning_ar: شخص يتظاهر بأنه يعرف أكثر من الجميع (مزعج)
expressions.meaning_en: an annoying person who acts as if they know everything
expressions.example: All right, clever clogs, you can do the maths yourself.

grammar.title: 'Dead' as an informal intensifier
grammar.explanation_ar: في العامية البريطانية تأتي dead قبل الصفة بمعنى very: dead tired، dead easy، dead hungry. لا تستخدمها في الكتابة الرسمية. وكلمات أخرى تقوّي الصفة: really، very، so.
grammar.explanation_en: In informal British English, 'dead' before an adjective means 'very': dead tired, dead easy, dead hungry. Don't use it in formal writing. Other intensifiers: really, very, so.
examples: Formal: The test was very easy.
